newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch police extend dead voodoo babies probe.
newsitem.headline: Dutch police extend dead voodoo babies probe.

text.p: Dutch police probing a macabre find of mummified infant remains hidden in voodoo dolls said on Saturday they were extending their investigation to the Dutch Caribbean and Surinam.
Police said they made the gruesome discovery while searching a house after arresting a man accused of raping a 44-year-old woman who died in suspicious circumstances last May.
Both the man and the woman practised voodoo, the witchcraft cult found in parts of the Caribbean and Africa, police said.
"The man involved came from Surinam and the woman from the Dutch Antilles so we will be looking in that region," Amsterdam police spokesman Klaas Wilting said.
Police said on Friday they had discovered the mummified parts of three new-born infants at the Amsterdam home of a Surinamese-born man.
"The police officers who made the find...are used to a lot, but they had never seen anything like this before," Wilting said. "They were badly shocked."
The 45-year-old man, identified only as 'Frits R', was arrested after his girlfriend was found dead and one of her daughters accused him of rape.
Daughters and neighbours of the dead woman told Dutch television on Saturday the man was a voodoo witchdoctor.
"He (Frits R.) was known as a medicine man," Glenda, a daughter of the dead woman, Marcelia de Groot, told local television on Saturday.
She said her mother had consulted Frits R. for depression after her husband died.
She become heavily influenced by him and later broke off relations with family and friends, Glenda said.
Another daughter, her face shielded from the camera, said Frits R. had treated her with ritual baths to eradicate "the voodoo on me."
De Groot, 44, was found dead at her north Amsterdam home in May after neighbours alerted police that she was missing. An autopsy later indicated she might have been poisoned.
The neighbours said De Groot and Frits R. had practised voodoo, an Afro-Caribbean cult based on strong ancestral links.

"She would phone me up at night and say she'd been stabbed," neighbour Ria Kraam told Dutch television. "When I went down she'd be lying trembling in her bed saying someone was stabbing her...that was the voodoo."
"They (Frits R. and the woman) were both involved in it," said Joke Lam, another neighbour.
Wilting told Reuters that no new witnesses had approached police since the case was publicised on Friday.
"The man himself has refused to make a statement beyond saying that he practises medicine," Wilting said.
